checkpoints.notes: 5 concepts brainstormed and scored (Echo Maze, Stack Attack: Tower Duel, Pulse Runner, Territory Ink, Orbit Duel: Rival Mode); Territory Ink selected for genre novelty vs. Cycle 1's Orbit Duel, Pulse Runner as fallback. Orbit Duel: Rival Mode carried forward as a future-cycle candidate rather than pursued now.

Single-file HTML5 canvas architecture: tick-based grid movement (110ms), BFS flood-fill territory capture on loop closure, lives-based win condition (3 lives), ordered collision-resolution rules, live-getter test hooks (window.__territoryInk) planned from the start to avoid Cycle 1's stale-snapshot bug. Documented scope cut: capture only claims neutral cells, not opponent territory.

Self-contained playable prototype implemented per docs/cycle2-design.md: grid movement, ordered per-tick collision resolution (bounds/head-on/self-crash/opponent trail-cut), BFS flood-fill capture, lives-based win/restart, HUD, and window.__territoryInk test hooks using live getters (board/players/gameOver/winner/tick) plus setDir()/restart()/forceCapture()/forceDie() helpers for deterministic automated testing. No build step, no external assets/deps.

Automated Playwright/headless-Chromium tests: all 6 tests / 19 assertions PASS (load+smoke, movement/trail, self-crash, flood-fill capture, opponent trail-cut, win condition + restart). Two issues found and fixed during test authoring (not gameplay bugs): (1) the first self-crash test path looped back through the player's own base and silently tested capture instead of a crash -- fixed by tracing a path that stays outside the base until it deliberately re-crosses its own trail, with a strict lives===before-1 assertion; (2) the win-condition test tried to reach 0 lives via real-time scripted deaths only, which hung because tick() halts tickCount once gameOver flips true -- fixed by adding a forceDie() test-only hook to drive the remaining deaths deterministically after proving one real death works. Fun/balance tuning and head-on collision are reasoned about but not covered by automated tests -- flagged as follow-ups.
